answer.evidence: In radon/visitors.py, ComplexityVisitor.__init__ (line ~157) takes no_assert=False and stores it at line 165. visit_Assert (lines ~257-260) does `self.complexity += not self.no_assert`, so a bool is added as 0 or 1: an assert adds 1 only when no_assert is False. Using a bool in arithmetic works but is implicit, so an explicit `if not self.no_assert:` would read more clearly. The flag is propagated to nested visitors at line 279 (ComplexityVisitor(off=False, no_assert=self.no_assert)) and line 313 (the class and function visitor construction), so nested blocks stay consistent. The comment at line 235 says "Ifs, with and assert statements count all as 1", which is stale next to the conditional behavior in visit_Assert. Review the tests that exercise no_assert, and check that every place that builds a visitor passes the flag. Other files get lighter checks: radon/complexity.py for the code that forwards no_assert, radon/raw.py and radon/metrics.py for any assert-related handling. A grep found none of the latter two, so they are low risk.
